As of the most recent evidence available, the current leader of al-Qaeda is Sayf al-Adl (also spelled Saif al-Adel/Seif al-Adel), who is believed to be operating as the group's de facto emir from Iran [d9][d7][d8]. Earlier sources described Ayman al-Zawahiri as al-Qaeda's "current leader" [d4][d6], but this information is outdated: Zawahiri was killed in a U.S. drone strike in Kabul on July 31, 2022 [d6][d1]. A United Nations report, confirmed by the U.S. State Department, concluded that Sayf al-Adl "is already operating as the de facto and uncontested leader of the group," with his location in Iran complicating a formal announcement of succession [d7][d2]. As of June 2024, al-Adl is still "believed to be al Qaeda's current overall emir," having succeeded Zawahiri, though neither al-Qaeda nor the Taliban has formally acknowledged Zawahiri's death or al-Adl's succession [d9].
